question: Should OpenClaw enforce plugin private-import boundaries at loader time as a fail-closed security boundary, and if so what exact runtime/resolution design and rollout proof are required before merge?
rationale: The PR changes a plugin compatibility and security boundary, but the current static implementation is bypassable and may break existing plugin setups; automation cannot choose the permanent boundary or rollout policy.

options.title: Redesign before merge
options.body: Require a robust resolver/runtime or AST-backed implementation with dependency traversal, normalized file handling, and fresh-install plus upgrade proof before landing.

options.title: Narrow to diagnostics first
options.body: Ship only a non-security lint/diagnostic path until maintainers are ready to enforce fail-closed runtime plugin loading.

options.title: Restart with a fresh design PR
options.body: Close or pause this stale branch and reopen the work after the desired security boundary and compatibility rollout are documented.

recommendation.title: Redesign before merge
recommendation.body: Require a robust resolver/runtime or AST-backed implementation with dependency traversal, normalized file handling, and fresh-install plus upgrade proof before landing.
